description: EarthPulse Labs is a solo team founded by Hafida Belayd, a computer science graduate passionate about data science, AI, and scientific storytelling. For NASA Space Apps 2026, I'm developing EarthPulse, an interactive tool that uses NASA Earth observation data, statistical analysis, and visualization to explore climate trends and make scientific insights more accessible.
summary: EarthPulse is an interactive climate investigation studio for students and the public. Explore four Moroccan locations on a 3D terrain map, compare annual and seasonal trends from NASA POWER, and see how accounting for time dependence changes the strength of the evidence. A paired comparison of Marrakech and Casablanca estimates how their temperature trends differ over 1991–2025. Visitors can inspect the method, switch between English and Arabic views, and download an Evidence Passport that records the result and its data sources.
details:
Did Marrakech warm faster than Casablanca? EarthPulse lets visitors investigate that question using the same 35 years of NASA POWER data (1991–2025). A 3D terrain explorer locates four Moroccan sites and shows the approximate scale of the MERRA-2 grid. The terrain provides geographic context; the app does not interpolate climate trends across it.

The first clue is Casablanca. Its grid warmed by an estimated +0.219 °C per decade. The conventional 95% interval excludes zero, but the cautious interval that accounts for residual time dependence (−0.026 to +0.465 °C per decade) includes it. To compare the cities directly, EarthPulse fits a trend to their paired annual temperature differences. The estimated Marrakech-minus-Casablanca trend is +0.263 °C per decade (exploratory 95% interval +0.144 to +0.382).

Visitors can test another question in Discovery & Seasons, which explores six climate variables across complete annual and seasonal records. English and Arabic analysis views explain the method, and a downloadable one-page Evidence Passport records the result and its sources. These estimates apply to the selected grids and period. The analysis does not establish causes, and seasonal and multi-variable comparisons are exploratory.

OpenAI Codex and Google's Gemini/Argon assisted with development, documentation, testing and presentation. Python calculates the reported results from the source data. The repository and data references are linked below.
